notes: §1985:XVI.1.4.3 GR1: an independent segment is in its initial state when 'Control is transferred to that segment as a result of the implicit transfer of control between consecutive statements from a segment with a different segment-number'. ProcedureTableBuilder.SegmentsPerPc gives each pc its segment-number, AlterSwitchEmitter.EmitSegmentState emits __SegOf, __seg and __EnterSegment (which returns the segment's alterable GO TOs to their written targets), and DispatchEmitter.EmitDispatchMethod tests __SegOf[__pc] != __seg on every pc the loop enters, so a fall-through from segment 10 into segment 50 resets it; segment-numbers reach here only at 85 (COBOL0902 refuses them at 2002, probed). The witness falls from a fixed section into SECTION 50 twice after an ALTER and sees INITIAL each time; probes seg1/seg4 at 85 also showed no reset on a same-segment PERFORM THRU (ALT ALT) or on the implicit return from a PERFORM of a fixed paragraph. Classes a, d, e, f do not reach a control-flow rule; b: segment-number 100 is COBOL6819. Aside: noncontiguous sections of one segment-number (§1985:XVI.1.2) compiled without a diagnostic; not this rule.

next.reason: 1985: "Control is transferred to that segment as a result of the implicit transfer of control between consecutive statements"; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds segmentation; candidates cover file ORGANIZATION, PERFORM, GO TO and other transfers, not segments". The rule belongs to the Segmentation module, for independent segments. No 2023 clause carries segments or segment-numbers, and the wording matches are unrelated, so the feature is dropped.
